children: The company will split the adjustment between direct price hikes and smaller packs, while quick commerce and premium personal care remain key areas of focus

Bajaj Consumer Care will raise consumer prices and reduce product pack sizes in the third quarter of FY27, targeting an overall price increase of around 5 per cent. The company plans to divide the adjustment roughly equally between direct price increases of 2-3 per cent and reductions in product grammage, as it seeks to manage input cost volatility while maintaining growth.

The proposed changes follow a calibrated price increase implemented towards the end of Q1 FY27, Managing Director Naveen Pandey said during the company's earnings call. The company is seeking to balance higher input costs with consumer affordability, rather than passing on the entire cost burden through direct price increases. Its pricing decisions come amid continued volatility in raw material prices.
“The cost environment remains volatile, and we stand committed to taking actions as appropriate to protect our P&L while being fair to our consumers,” Pandey said.

The pricing decision follows a rise in revenue and profitability in the September quarter. Bajaj Consumer Care's revenue from operations increased 25.5 per cent year on year to Rs 332.83 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 265.27 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Net profit rose 65.9 per cent to Rs 70.15 crore from Rs 42.29 crore.
General Trade And Organised Retail Grow In Mid-20% Range

The company recorded growth in the mid-20 per cent range across general trade and organised retail during the quarter, according to Pandey. Within general trade, rural markets continued to grow marginally faster than urban markets. Modern trade and e-commerce also reported growth across their respective sub-channels and customer segments, indicating that the performance extended across multiple distribution channels.

Bajaj Consumer Care is following a differentiated approach to quick commerce, depending on the brand and market. For established products with wide distribution, the company views the channel primarily as a way to meet existing consumer demand and improve convenience. For premium products, it also sees an opportunity to attract new customers and increase product discovery.
“For very large and very well-distributed brands like Almond Drops, the channel would be a demand fulfillment channel, providing convenience to the consumer,” Pandey said.

The company intends to use quick commerce for demand generation as well as fulfilment for selected premium and urban-focused products, including serums and other higher-end personal care offerings. Rather than adopting a single strategy across its portfolio, Bajaj Consumer Care will determine the role of the channel according to individual brands and markets. Pandey identified quick commerce as the fastest-growing sub-channel within organised trade.

Alongside its expansion across retail channels, the company is continuing to strengthen distribution through its Aarohan programme. Following the completion of the first phase, Aarohan 2.0 will focus on expanding direct reach and improving execution, Pandey said. The distribution initiative forms part of the company's efforts to increase product availability while building on growth across general trade and organised retail.
Advertising Spending Rises 18.1% In First Half

Bajaj Consumer Care's advertising and sales promotion expenses rose 7.1 per cent year on year to Rs 41.65 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 38.89 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26. However, spending declined 16.7 per cent sequentially from Rs 50.01 crore in Q1 FY27, indicating lower expenditure during the September quarter than in the preceding three-month period.

For the six months ended September 30, 2026, advertising and sales promotion expenses increased 18.1 per cent to Rs 91.66 crore from Rs 77.75 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations during the first half rose 25.2 per cent to Rs 674.40 crore, compared with Rs 538.66 crore in the corresponding period last year, while net profit increased 74.9 per cent to Rs 140.90 crore from Rs 80.57 crore.

In Q2 FY27, total expenses increased 14.9 per cent to Rs 254.68 crore, below the 25.5 per cent growth in revenue from operations. Profit before tax rose 68.7 per cent to Rs 86.76 crore from Rs 51.43 crore in the year-ago quarter. The figures show that revenue and profit grew faster than total expenses during the quarter, even as the company continued to face input cost volatility.
Core Category Remains A Growth Priority

Pandey said the company continues to see opportunities in its core category, which has a penetration of more than 91 per cent across Indian households. He estimated that demographic shifts and changing consumer preferences of the kind discussed during the earnings interaction affect less than 1 per cent to 1.5 per cent of households nationally. The company therefore intends to pursue growth in its existing category while responding to changes in consumer demand.

While acknowledging premiumisation and evolving preferences in certain segments, Pandey said improving product appeal and strengthening distribution remain priorities. The company plans to participate in the shift towards premium products without treating changing preferences as a uniform trend across the entire category. Its approach combines efforts to make products more appealing with improvements in availability across markets and retail channels.
“At an overall level, I think there is a lot of job to be done on our end in terms of making the product and the category exciting, and ensuring greater quality distribution,” Pandey said.

For the remainder of FY27, pricing, distribution and channel-specific strategies will remain central to the company's efforts to sustain growth amid cost volatility. Bajaj Consumer Care's first-half revenue rose 25.2 per cent and net profit increased 74.9 per cent, while its planned Q3 price and pack-size adjustments are intended to address input cost pressures. The company has also identified premium personal care products and quick commerce as areas for differentiated growth strategies.
